questions.question: Which natural disaster triggered storms, flash floods, and landslips in the northeastern states of India in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cyclone Remal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cyclone Remal** was a significant weather event that caused extensive damage in the northeastern states of India in 2024.
 
• The cyclone brought about severe **storms, flash floods, and landslips** in the region, leading to widespread disruption.
 
• It was among the most destructive cyclones to hit the northeastern part of India in recent history, impacting thousands of lives and properties.
 
• Emergency response teams were deployed to assist in rescue and relief operations, highlighting the importance of disaster preparedness and management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cyclones:**

 
 
• A cyclone is a large scale air mass that rotates around a strong center of low atmospheric pressure.
 
• Cyclones are characterized by inward spiraling winds that rotate counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• They are classified into different types such as tropical cyclones, extratropical cyclones, and subtropical cyclones based on their formation and characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Flash Floods:**
 
 
• Flash floods are rapid flooding of low-lying areas: washes, rivers, dry lakes, and basins.
 
• They are caused by heavy rain associated with a severe thunderstorm, hurricane, or cyclone.
 
• Flash floods can occur within minutes or hours of heavy rainfall, and can also occur when dams or levees break.
 
 
 
• **Landslips:**
 
 
• Landslips, also known as landslides, involve the movement of rock, earth, or debris down a sloped section of land.
 
• They are often caused by rainfall, earthquakes, volcanic activity, or other factors that make the slope unstable.
 
• Landslips can cause significant damage to infrastructure, property, and can also result in loss of life.

questions.question: In the Union Budget 2024, which initiative did the Finance Minister announce to enhance productivity in agriculture?

options.text: A new subsidy program for farmers

questions.solution:

• GM crops are plants used in agriculture, the DNA of which has been modified using genetic engineering techniques.
 
• The primary aim of developing GM crops is to introduce new traits such as resistance to pests, diseases, environmental conditions, and reduction of spoilage, or to enhance the nutritional value of the crop.
 
• While GM crops have the potential to increase agricultural productivity, there are concerns related to environmental impacts and food safety.

• Expansion of irrigation facilities includes the construction of dams, canals, and water reservoirs to ensure a steady supply of water to agricultural fields.
 
• Efficient irrigation systems can significantly increase crop yields and reduce dependence on unpredictable rainfall.

• Comprehensive reviews of the agricultural research setup aim to identify gaps, improve research quality, and ensure that research findings are effectively translated into practice.
 
• Investing in agricultural research can lead to innovations that address challenges such as climate change, pest resistance, and soil degradation.

questions.question: The M72/AS01E vaccine candidate launched in 2024 almost after a century of BCG vaccine discovery is effective against which of the following diseases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tuberculosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The M72/AS01E vaccine candidate has been developed to provide protection against **Tuberculosis (TB)**, a bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
 
• It was launched in 2024, almost a century after the discovery of the BCG vaccine, which has been used since 1921 to prevent TB.
 
• Clinical trials of the M72/AS01E vaccine showed significant efficacy in preventing active pulmonary TB in adults.
 
• This vaccine represents a major advancement in the fight against TB, especially in regions with high TB incidence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tuberculosis (TB)**

 
 
• TB is a contagious bacterial infection that primarily affects the lungs but can spread to other organs.
 
• It spreads through the air when a person with active TB coughs or sneezes.
 
• Common symptoms include a persistent cough, chest pain, and coughing up blood.
 
• Effective treatment typically involves a combination of antibiotics taken for at least six months.
 
 
 
• **BCG Vaccine**
 
 
• The Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine is the only currently available vaccine for TB.
 
• It is administered primarily to infants and children in countries with high TB prevalence.
 
• The BCG vaccine is known to protect against severe forms of TB in children, such as TB meningitis and miliary TB.
 
 
 
• **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**
 
 
• It is the bacterium that causes tuberculosis.
 
• It is a slow-growing pathogen that can remain dormant in the body for years before causing active disease.
 
• Diagnosis of TB infection is often done through a skin test (Mantoux test) or blood tests, followed by chest X-rays and sputum tests for confirmation.
 
 
 
• **Global TB Burden**
 
 
• TB is one of the top 10 causes of death worldwide and a leading cause of death from a single infectious agent.
 
• According to the World Health Organization (WHO), millions of new TB cases occur annually, with the highest burden in developing countries.
 
• Efforts to control TB include vaccination, early diagnosis, effective treatment, and public health initiatives aimed at reducing transmission.

questions.question: Which of the following languages were added to the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution by the 71st Amendment Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri, Konkani, and Nepali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 71st Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution was enacted in 1992.
 
• This amendment added three languages to the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The languages included were **Manipuri, Konkani, and Nepali**.
 
• The Eighth Schedule lists the official languages recognized by the Indian Constitution.
 
• With the addition of these three languages, the total number of languages in the Eighth Schedule increased to 18.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• The Eighth Schedule to the Indian Constitution contains a list of 22 scheduled languages.
 
• The languages are recognized by the Constitution for their importance and are used for official purposes.
 
• Initially, the Eighth Schedule included 14 languages, which has since been expanded through subsequent amendments.
 
• The languages listed in the Eighth Schedule are also entitled to representation on the Official Languages Commission.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments**
 
 
• Amendments to the Constitution are changes or additions made to the country's founding legal document.

questions.question: The Citizenship Amendment Act was enacted in 2019 and was operationalised after the rules for it were notified by the Ministry of Home Affairs on _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11 March 2024**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) was enacted on 12 December 2019.
 
• The CAA aims to provide Indian citizenship to persecuted minorities from Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Afghanistan.
 
• The act focuses on granting citizenship to Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians from these countries.
 
• The Ministry of Home Affairs notified the rules for the CAA, which operationalized the act, on 11 March 2024.
 
• The act has been a subject of significant debate and controversy within India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA)**

 
 
• It amends the Citizenship Act, 1955 to make illegal migrants from certain religious communities eligible for Indian citizenship.
 
• The act applies to Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians who entered India on or before 31 December 2014.
 
• It reduces the requirement of residence in India for citizenship from 11 years to 5 years for these migrants.
 
• The act does not extend to Muslims from these countries, which has led to widespread protests and opposition.
 
 
 
• **National Population Register (NPR)**
 
 
• The NPR is a register of all the usual residents of the country.
 
• It is prepared at the local (village/sub-town), sub-district, district, state, and national levels under the provisions of the Citizenship Act 1955 and the Citizenship Rules, 2003.
 
• The objective of the NPR is to create a comprehensive identity database of every usual resident in the country.
 
• The data for the NPR was first collected in 2010 and updated in 2015 through a door-to-door survey.
 
 
 
• **National Register of Citizens (NRC)**
 
 
• The NRC is a register containing names of all genuine Indian citizens.
 
• It was first prepared after the 1951 Census of India and since then it has not been updated until recently in Assam.
 
• The NRC process in Assam was aimed at identifying illegal immigrants in the state.
 
• The final NRC list for Assam was published on 31 August 2019.
 
 
 
• **Foreigners Tribunal**
 
 
• Foreigners Tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies established in India to determine if a person staying illegally in the country is a foreigner or not.
 
• These tribunals are unique to Assam and have been established under the Foreigners Act, 1946 and the Foreigners (Tribunal) Order, 1964.
 
• They play a crucial role in the identification and deportation process of illegal immigrants.
 
• The tribunals have been a subject of scrutiny and criticism regarding their functioning and decisions.
